subject: Are two and three factors models non-nested?

messages.author: 478086b2fcb52506
messages.subject: Are two and three factors models non-nested?
parts:
Dear All,

I have these two CFA models:

HS.model1 <- ' f1  =~  A3 + A6 +  A9 
f2  =~ A2 + A5 + A8
f3 =~ A1 + A4 + A7
'

HS.model2 <- ' f1  =~  A3 + A6 +  A9 
f2  =~ A1 + A2 + A4 + A5 + A7 + A8
'
For me these two models are non-nested, so they should be compared using BICs. Is it correct?

Thanks in advance,
Alberto

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Are two and three factors models non-nested?
parts: For me these two models are non-nested, so they should be compared using BICs. Is it correct?

They actually are nested, because the 2-factor model is equivalent to the 3-factor model if you constrain the factors to be perfectly correlated.  So you can use the anova() function to get a chi-squared difference test.   But you can also use AIC and BIC for nested OR non-nested models.

Terry
